headline: Structure-based protein-ligand tools gain speed and face new benchmarks
label: Structural Computation Software Tools
summary: Co-folding and AI docking models now sit beside classical methods, prompting prospective and pocket-level benchmarks of binding predictions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational tooling for protein-ligand structure and energetics, with emphasis on how well these tools perform and how fast they run. Several items are benchmarks: a prospective evaluation of AF3, Boltz-2 and Chai-1 co-folding on 489 SARS-CoV-2 Mac1 ligand complexes against DOCK3.7 docking; a free energy comparison of MM/PBSA, FEP and PMF for PARP1 versus PARP2 selectivity; and Bento's evaluation of 11 classical, deep learning, and co-folding tools on drug-design data. Others target throughput: FlashAffinity reports a 50x inference speedup over Boltz-2, NeuralMD accelerates binding molecular dynamics with a physics-informed surrogate, and pyDelPhi offers a Python/Numba Poisson-Boltzmann framework with a CUDA backend. The AML drug generation preprint is less directly comparable, using AlphaFold3-modeled targets and docking-tested ligands. What is new is the pairing of prospective, head-to-head evaluation with surrogate models built for speed; the abstracts do not establish cross-tool rankings.
